sources.text:
Police to provide more appointment times for passport and ID card applicants - Finnish Government

# Police to provide more appointment times for passport and ID card applicants

 Publication date 15.4.2025 13.04 

The police are addressing efficient licensing services by increasing the number of appointments for passport and identity card customers. Save time and money by booking an appointment easily online.

Police licensing services nationwide have a goal to encourage more customers to make an appointment when interacting with the police. 

“To achieve this goal, police licensing services will increase the number of appointments for customers. We recommend that all customers book an appointment rather than just turning up at a police station,” says Hanna Piipponen, Chief of Licence Administration at the National Police Board.

## You can find more slots on the website

More appointment times will be available to passport and ID card applicants. Appointment times can also be found beyond the opening hours of the police station. The police will add more slots to the booking system on a daily and weekly basis, depending on the police station. 

If you can’t find a suitable time straight away, check out the situation later. 

You can freely choose the most convenient police station for you anywhere in Finland. You can find available appointments and service points at: asiointi.poliisi.fi 

“When applicants initiate their passport or ID card application online, the system automatically directs them to appointment booking if they need to visit a police station in person,” says Hanna Piipponen.

Initiating an application online in advance makes for quick, effortless contact rather than having to perhaps wait in a queue for hours without an appointment. If you need to visit a police station for identification purposes, you can complete your visit in less than ten minutes with an appointment.

## Deal with permit and licensing matters on line – easily and at a lower cost

Increasingly more permit and licensing matters can be initiated or even completed online. It’s not even always necessary to visit a police station at all for some permit and licensing matters, and nor does use of the service depend on office hours. This means it pays to initiate an application electronically whenever possible from the customer's perspective. 

Identity cards and passports are cheaper when initiated online. 

Book an appointment online and avoid queuing. You can plan in advance when you interact and how you will spend your time.

### Finnish Government

Snellmaninkatu 1 A, Helsinki

PO Box 23, FI-00023 Government, Finland

Tel. +358 295 16001

sources.title: ”Vastaavaa ruuhkaa ei ole ennen nähty” – passia voi joutua odottamaan Helsingissä kuusi viikkoa | Demokraatti.fi
highlights:
## 4.3.2022 10:40 ・ Päivitetty: 4.3.2022 10:40

# ”Vastaavaa ruuhkaa ei ole ennen nähty” – passia voi joutua odottamaan Helsingissä kuusi viikkoa

Helsingin poliisilaitoksen lupapalveluissa joudutaan säännöstelemään sisään otettavien asiakkaiden määrää.

Lupapalveluissa osoitteessa Pasilanraitio 11 on tänään perjantaina ollut ennennäkemätön ruuhka. Asiakkaat voivat joutua jonottamaan vuoroaan ulkona ja jonotusaika saattaa venyä yli kahteen tuntiin.

– Jos ei ole aivan pakottavaa tarvetta hakea passia nyt, niin ei kannata tulla tänään paikan päälle. Koko viikon meillä on ollut kova ruuhka, 800 asiakasta päivässä. Tänään asiakkaita on ollut aamusta lähtien niin paljon, että vastaavaa ruuhkaa ei ole ennen nähty, ylikomisario Pekka Kallio toteaa tiedotteessa.

Lupapalveluiden henkilöstö palvelee sekä ajanvarauksella että vuoronumerolla asioivia asiakkaita.

Ajanvarauksen kautta sovitun ajan henkilökortin tai passin uusimiseen saa Helsingissä tällä hetkellä kuuden viikon päähän.

Poliisin mukaan ajanvaraukseen vapautuu myös peruutusaikoja ja viikon alussa myönnetään aikoja viikonlopuille, joten asiakkaiden kannattaa seurata tilannetta aktiivisesti poliisi.fi-sivuilta Ajanvaraus | Poliisin sähköinen asiointi

sources.title: First 30 Days in Finland: The Complete Expat Checklist | NordicExpat
highlights:
Apply at DVV once you have a henkilötunnus and kotikunta — takes 2–4 weeks; apply in week 3–4

...

Everything in Finland eventually traces back to your henkilötunnus — the Finnish

...

The henkilötunnus is issued by the DVV (Digi- ja väestötietovirasto, the Digital and Population Data Services Agency) when you register as a foreign national. There are two steps: submit the online foreigner registration form at dvv.fi, then attend an in-person appointment at a DVV service point.

The in-person appointment is the bottleneck. Wait times vary — in Helsinki they can stretch to a few weeks during busy periods. Book the appointment the day you land, even if you submit the form later.

...

Book an in-person appointment — walk-ins are rarely accepted. Expect a wait of a few days to a week. During the appointment, the bank will also issue your pankkitunnukset (online banking credentials), which is a separate and critical item covered below.

...

## Week 4: Finnish ID Card, Suomi.fi, and Tax Card Review

### Apply for your Finnish identity card

A Finnish henkilökortti (identity card) is not strictly required — you can use your passport or EU ID card indefinitely — but it is a practical document to have. It is accepted as ID everywhere in Finland, fits in a wallet, is cheaper to replace than a passport, and is the credential some government services prefer for strong identification.

Apply in person at a DVV service point. Processing takes 2–4 weeks, which is why you apply in week 4 rather than waiting. The card will arrive within your first two months if you apply now.

What you need:

- Your passport or current EU identity card
- Your henkilötunnus
- A confirmed municipality of residence registered with DVV
- The application fee (check the current amount at dvv.fi — fees are updated periodically)

Children under 15 need a guardian present. There is no minimum age requirement.

...

DVV appointment wait is too long. DVV service point wait times vary significantly by city. Helsinki is the worst; Espoo, Vantaa, and smaller cities are often faster. If you have flexibility, check DVV's online booking system for all service points within commuting distance and book at whichever has the earliest slot.

...

By the end of day 30, you should have:

...

- Finnish bank account open with pankkitunnukset active
- Kela application submitted; Kelakortti requested

...

- Finnish SIM on a contract plan
- Registered at terveyskeskus in your municipality

...

- Finnish ID card application submitted at DVV

...

How soon can I apply for a Finnish ID card?

You can apply for a Finnish identity card (henkilökortti) at a DVV service point once you have a henkilötunnus and a registered municipality of residence. The card takes 2–4 weeks to arrive, so apply in week 3 or 4 to have it within your first two months.

sources.title: I tillståndstjänsterna vid Polisinrättningen i Helsingfors har öppnats rikligt med tidsbeställningstider för vårmånaderna - Statsrådet
highlights:
Utgivningsdatum 31.1.2025 9.23 

Gör dig redo för vårens och sommarens resor i god tid genom att förnya ditt pass eller identitetskort som går ut. Utan tidsbokning kan du identifiera dig vid tillståndstjänsterna i Helsingfors i allmänhet på mindre än en timme. När du bokar tid får hanteringen av ditt ärende snabbare.

Det lönar sig alltid att inleda ansökan av ett nytt resedokument på webben på adressen poliisi.fi. Att förnya ditt pass eller identitetskort kräver inte alltid ett besök på polisstationen. Polisens elektroniska ärendehanteringssystem meddelar om du behöver besöka polisstationen för att identifiera dig.

Identifieringen kan göras antingen genom att boka en tid i förväg eller genom att köa till en tillståndsenhet utan tidsbokning. I Helsingfors betjänar polisens tillståndsenhet på huvudpolisstationen i Böle.

Efterfrågan på resedokument är alltid störst före semesterperioder. Du kan förbereda dig för vårens och sommarens resor i god tid i förväg genom att boka en tid till polisstationen för att förnya ditt pass- eller identitetskort. Ett stort antal tidsbeställningstider för vårmånaderna har nu öppnats vid tillståndsenheten i Böle.

– Det är en bra idé att boka tid i förväg, eftersom de som köar för att sköta ärenden får vänta i en dryg halvtimme i genomsnitt. Under dagar eller tider då det är rusning kan väntetiden bli längre, säger kommissarie Satu Mäkinen vid funktionen Tillståndsärenden vid polisen i Helsingfors.

I allmänhet har tillståndstjänsterna i Böle det största antalet kunder på måndagar och fredagar. De livligaste tiderna på dagen är öppnings- och stängningstiderna, klockan 8.00 och 16.00, samt lunchtid mellan klockan 11.00 och 13.00 .

...

I den elektroniska ärendehanteringstjänsten kan du välja från vilket avhämtningsställe du vill hämta ditt färdiga pass eller identitetskort. Du ska ha med dig försändelsekoden i ankomstmeddelandet, och ett pass eller identitetskort som utfärdats av en finsk myndighet. Ett pass eller identitetskort vars giltighetstid gått ut för mindre än ett år sedan duger också för att styrka din identitet.

Du kan ge fullmakt åt en annan person för att denna avhämtar ditt pass. Då måste personen som avhämtar passet ha med sig fullmakt, försändelsekod och ett giltigt finländskt pass eller identitetskort. Fullmaktsmallen kan skrivas ut till exempel från polisens webbplats: Leverans av pass.

# Gör så här när du behöver ett nytt pass eller identitetskort

- Innan du ansöker om pass eller identitetskort ska du ta reda på vilken typ av resedokument du behöver för resmålet. Du kan resa till EU-länderna och några andra europeiska länder utöver med pass även med identitetskort.
- Gå på passfotografering. Fotot som fogas till passansökan får vara högst 6 månader gammalt.
- Börja med ansökan av pass eller identitetskort i polisens elektroniska ärendehanteringssystem. Om du inte kan ansöka om resedokument på nätet, kan du lämna in din ansökan på polisstationen. Det är billigare och snabbare att lämna in ansökan på nätet.
- Identifiera dig vid behov på polisstationen genom att antingen i förväg reservera tid på nätet för att identifiera dig eller genom att köa med könummer.
- Kom ihåg att avbeställa tiden som du bokat till tillståndstjänsterna om du inte kan närvara.
- Pass, identitetskort och tillstånd
- Polisinrättningen i Helsingfors, verksamhetsställen och tjänster

sources.title: Finnish ID Card for Foreigners (Ulkomaalaisen Henkilökortti)
highlights:
Foreigners who live in Finland can get a Finnish identity card from the police, called the foreigner's identity card (ulkomaalaisen henkilökortti). The rules sit in the Identity Card Act (henkilökorttilaki 663/2016): you need a valid residence permit or residence card (or a registered right of residence), a municipality of residence (kotikunta) in Finland, and your details in the Population Information System. In 2026 the card costs EUR 59, or EUR 53 if you apply electronically.

...

Two things set the foreigner's card apart:

- It is not a travel document. The Act requires the foreigner's identity card to carry a note that it cannot be used as a travel document (§ 4). For travel you still need your passport.
- It follows your permit. It is issued for five years, but never for longer than your residence permit or residence card is valid (§ 19).

...

Section 14 of the Identity Card Act lists three conditions for a foreigner's identity card, on top of the Act's general rules:

1. You have a valid residence permit or residence card, or your right of residence has been registered (for EU citizens, see our EU registration guide).
2. You have a municipality of residence (kotikunta) in Finland under the Municipality of Residence Act.
3. Your details have been entered in the Population Information System.

Conditions 2 and 3 mean the card comes after your population registration. If you have not registered yet, start with our guides to DVV registration and the Finnish personal identity code. Non-EU citizens who are still waiting for a permit should read our residence permit guide first.

...

Check the current fee with the police (poliisi.fi)

...

Under the Act, identity cards are applied for from the police, and the application can be started electronically (henkilökorttilaki § 9). The 2026 fee table charges less for an electronic application.

### Visit in person, at least the first time

The applicant must come in person to complete the application. For a foreigner's identity card, the Act lets you skip the visit only if all of these apply (§ 10):

- you were issued a foreigner's identity card within the previous six years, and you visited the authority in person for that application,
- you were over 12 when that card was issued, and
- you gave a signature sample within the previous six years and your surname or first name has not changed since.

The police can still ask you to come in to identify you, give a new signature sample or for another special reason. In practice, your first foreigner's identity card means a visit.

### Bring ID, give fingerprints

You must show a valid identity document, such as your passport. If you have none, a foreigner must show a valid residence permit card or residence card, and the police may compare your fingerprints with those stored on it (§ 11). Fingerprints are taken from everyone applying for an identity card, except applicants under 12 or people who cannot give them because of age, disability, illness or a similar reason (§ 9 a).

### Receive the card

The card is sent as a registered letter or a similar trackable item (§ 21). In special cases the police hand it over instead. Your previous identity card stops being valid when the new card is handed over to you.

...

The Act says an identity card includes the citizen certificate (kansalaisvarmenne) issued by DVV, which is used for electronic identification. The minor's identity card and the temporary identity card do not include it (§ 3). For how certificate cards work with Suomi.fi services, see our Suomi.fi e-identification guide.

An amendment in force from 1 October 2026 (823/2026) adds that the foreigner's identity card includes the right to take into use the digital identity document under the separate Act on digital identity documents (812/2026) (§ 1 a).

## When the card is cancelled

Section 26 lists when a foreigner's identity card is revoked. The ones most likely to affect you:

- your residence permit, registered right of residence or residence card is revoked, or you are deported,
- you no longer have a municipality of residence in Finland,
- you ask for it to be cancelled, or
- you report it lost or stolen.

If you move away from Finland and no longer have a municipality of residence here, the Act says the card is revoked.

## Common problems and fixes

- "The police said I have no municipality of residence." The card requires a kotikunta. Our DVV registration guide explains population registration.
- "My card expires when my permit does." That is the rule: the Act caps the card at the validity of your residence permit or residence card.
- "I tried to travel with it." The foreigner's card is marked as not valid for travel. Carry your passport.
- "My old card stopped working." The previous card's validity ends when the new card is handed over to you.

## Your next step

Confirm you have a residence permit (or registered right of residence), a municipality of residence, and your details in the Population Information System. Then start the application with the police, who handle identity cards (henkilökorttilaki § 9); their website is poliisi.fi. If you have strong electronic identification (see our guide to Finnish online banking IDs), you can apply online for the lower fee. Then book your in-person visit.

sources.title: Passports and identity cards can be quickly renewed by queuing in Helsinki - Finnish Government
highlights:
Before applying for a passport or identity card, identify what travel document you will need at your destination. Does the passport have to remain valid for a certain period after your trip? Do you need a visa?

You only need an identity card when going to the EU member states and a few other European countries. As a rule, travel documents are not checked when crossing the border in Schengen countries, but you need to show it when asked to do so. While no travel documents are needed when travelling in the Nordic countries, you need to prove your identity at request.

“The quickest way to get a new passport or identity card is to complete the application online and identify yourself in the licence services of the Helsinki Police Department if required. The typical waiting time with a queue number is 30–60 minutes. The busiest hours are at 8 am, between 11 am and 1 pm, and at 4 pm. Lunch hours are the most congested,” says Chief Inspector Satu Mäkinen.

If you cannot or do not want to apply for a passport or identity card online, you can also complete an application at a police station. Online applications are quicker and carry a lower charge.

## Instructions for applying for travel documents in Helsinki

- Before applying for a passport or identity card, identify what travel document you will need at your destination. You only need an identity card when going to the EU member states and a few other European countries.
- Start to apply for a passport or identity card online.
- Identify yourself at a police station if required. The quickest way to identify yourself is to use the queue number system. 
- Remember to cancel your booked appointment if you are unable to show up.
- Passports, identity cards and permits - Police (poliisi.fi)
- Helsinki Police Department, units and services - Police (poliisi.fi)

sources.title: Many new appointments made available in the Helsinki Police Department’s licence services for the spring - Finnish Government
highlights:
Get ready for spring and summer travels well beforehand by applying for a new passport and identity card. Without any appointment, your identity will usually be verified in the Helsinki Police Department’s licence services in less than an hour. If you book an appointment, the process will be quicker.

You should always apply for a new travel document online at poliisi.fi. To have a new passport or identity card, you do not always need to visit a police station. The police’s online services will tell you if you need to visit a police station to verify your identity.

You can have your identity verified by booking an appointment or visiting licence services without any appointment. The Helsinki Police Department’s licence services are at the central police station in Pasila.

Demand for travel documents is always highest before holiday seasons. You can get ready for your spring and summer travels by booking an appointment for a new passport or identity card at the police station. Many new appointments have been made available in the Pasila licence services for the spring.

“We recommend that you book an appointment, because without it, you may have to wait for more than half an hour. During busiest days and hours, the waiting time may be longer,” says Chief Inspector Satu Mäkinen from the Helsinki Police Department’s licence services.

Typically, the Pasila licence services have the highest number of customers on Mondays and Fridays. The busiest hours are around opening and closing times at 8 am and 4 pm, as well as around lunch hours from 11 am to 1 pm.

# Keep your previous travel document to pick up your new one

In the online services, you can choose the location from which to pick up your new passport or identity card. When picking up your new travel document, you need the delivery ID included in the pick-up notification, as well as a passport or identity card granted by a Finnish authority. You can use a passport or identity card expired less than a year ago to prove your identity.

You can also authorise another person to pick up your passport. In this case, the person who picks up your passport requires a power of attorney, the delivery ID and a valid Finnish passport or identity card. You can print a template of a power of attorney on the police’s website: Passport delivery.

# Do this when you need a new passport or identity card

- Before applying for a passport or identity card, identify what travel document you will need at your destination. You can travel to the EU member states and a few other European countries with a passport or an identity card.
- Have your passport photo taken. The photo attached to your passport application cannot be older than six months.
- Apply for a passport or identity card in the police’s online services. If you cannot apply for a travel document online, you can also complete an application at a police station. Online applications are quicker and carry a lower charge.
- If required, verify your identity at a police station by booking an appointment or using the queue number system.
- Remember to cancel your appointment if you cannot make it.
- Passports, identity cards and permits
- Helsinki Police Department, units and services

sources.title: Finnish identity card
highlights:
The Finnish identity card (Finnish: henkilökortti; Swedish: identitetskort) is one of two official identity documents in Finland, the other being the Finnish passport. Any citizen or resident can get an identification card. [3] Finnish citizens will get indication of citizenship on the card. It is available as an electronic ID card (Finnish: sähköinen henkilökortti; Swedish: elektroniskt identitetskort), which enables logging into certain services on the Internet, local computers or adding digital signatures into LibreOffice ODF documents or creating DigiDoc formatted containers that also allows encryption during content transfer. ID card is applied at a police station and it is issued by the police. 

Possession of an ID card or any ID document is non-compulsory in Finland, though interactions with officials and companies, like voting, picking up a parcel from Posti offices or buying alcohol when a salesperson suspects buyer to be under 18 or 30 years old, can be difficult or impossible without an ID card, a passport or a driving licence.

sources.title: Poliisi muistuttaa: tarkista passin ja henkilökortin voimassaolo ennen syksyn ja talven matkoja - Mediamaailma
highlights:
Helsingin poliisilaitos kehottaa matkailijoita tarkistamaan passin tai henkilökortin voimassaolon hyvissä ajoin ennen ulkomaanmatkaa. Poliisin lupapalveluissa on tällä hetkellä runsaasti vapaita ajanvarausaikoja, ja asiointi onnistuu nopeimmillaan jo saman tai seuraavan päivän aikana.

Hakemus kannattaa tehdä verkossa poliisin asiointipalvelussa, jossa matkustusasiakirjan hinta on myös hieman edullisempi kuin poliisiasemalla. Jos järjestelmä ohjaa tunnistautumaan poliisiasemalle, ajan voi varata helposti sähköisen ajanvarausjärjestelmän kautta.

– Suosittelemme ajanvarauksen tekemistä etukäteen. Ilman varausta voi joutua jonottamaan päivästä ja kellonajasta riippuen jopa yli tunnin, kertoo Helsingin poliisilaitoksen lupa-asioista vastaava ylikomisario Jari Friman.

...

#### Näin uusit passin tai henkilökortin

1. Käy kuvattavana. Hakemukseen liitettävä kuva saa olla enintään 6 kuukautta vanha.
2. Aloita hakemus osoitteessa asiointi.poliisi.fi Jos järjestelmä vaatii tunnistautumista poliisiasemalla, varaa aika etukäteen ja muista perua se, jos et pääse paikalle.
